name: Storm Journey
bestFor: League bowlers who need angle and carry
bowlerMatch: Medium to high rev players opening the lane
layoutTip: Use 5 inch pin for cleaner fronts and stronger continuation.
summary: Top-tier house-shot scorer with easy length and a hard-driving backend.

name: Hammer Black Widow 3.0
bestFor: Players wanting a strong benchmark for house
laneMatch: Fresh to blended medium-heavy house conditions
bowlerMatch: Tweeners and crankers with medium speed
layoutTip: Benchmark around 55 x 4.5 x 35 to blend wet/dry.
summary: A proven heavy-hitter for league blocks where miss-room and hit are both required.

name: Motiv Pride Liberty
bowlerMatch: Higher speed players who need help turning the corner
layoutTip: Polish can add pop; scuff to 3000 to blend overreaction.
summary: Great blend of control and angle for players who need continuation without chaos.
cons: Can be too angular for lower rev rates

name: 900 Global Sublime Focus
layoutTip: A 4.5 inch pin keeps reaction readable through transition.
summary: A confidence benchmark for starting league sets and reading transition quickly.
pros: Good blend of traction and backend
cons: Not as angular as true skid/flip pieces
May read too early on low-volume houses

name: Roto Grip Attention Star S2
bestFor: League players creating deep inside angle
laneMatch: Transitioned house shots with spot-downlane shape
bowlerMatch: Rev-dominant or lower speed power styles
layoutTip: Longer pin helps preserve energy if fronts go.
summary: High-octane ball for opening up the lane and keeping strikes flowing in game three.
cons: Can be too much in dry fronts

name: Track Theorem Pearl
bestFor: League players balancing control and angle
laneMatch: Medium house patterns with cliffed wet/dry
bowlerMatch: Tweeners and strokers wanting cleaner shape
layoutTip: Use medium VAL angle to avoid over-jump.
summary: A cleaner look that still stores enough power for modern house-shot carry.
cons: Can be too clean for higher speed on volume

name: Brunswick Vaporize
bestFor: House players needing continuation on carrydown
layoutTip: Touch with 2000 if it misses the spot downlane.
summary: Useful second-ball look after stronger solids start reading too early.
cons: Not ideal on very dry league surfaces

name: Hammer Effect Tour
bestFor: League bowlers wanting smooth but strong
bowlerMatch: All styles; especially balanced speed/rev players
layoutTip: 4.25 pin and moderate VAL gives clean benchmark read.
summary: Dependable benchmark motion with enough hit to remain in play deep into league blocks.
cons: Can blend too much for very high rev players

name: Motiv Hyper Venom
bowlerMatch: Medium speed and rev styles wanting continuation
layoutTip: Keep surface high to preserve length.
summary: Strong transition choice that lets you move in without losing hit.

name: Ebonite The One Reverb
bestFor: League bowlers needing stronger downlane shape
bowlerMatch: Players with forward roll needing angle
layoutTip: Use a longer pin-to-PAP for cleaner entry through the heads.
summary: A useful angular option when benchmark shapes start leaving weak corners.
cons: Needs touch for lower speed styles
